title: Isaiah 13 — The oracle concerning Babylon: the host from the end of the skies and the day of YHWH

citations: Weis, A Definition of the Genre Maśśāʾ (1986)
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed vs ASV 'burden'. maśśāʾ bāḇel ʾăšer ḥāzāh yᵉšaʿyāhû ben-ʾāmôṣ: the heading noun is maśśāʾ II 'pronouncement', so 'oracle' is the lexical consensus (NRSV); 'burden' and the Jer 23 pun are fairly reported.
ʿal har-nišpeh śᵉʾû-nēs ... pitḥê nᵉḏîḇîm: 'bare mountain', 'signal', 'gates of the nobles' are exact; the jussive wᵉyāḇōʾû as purpose ('that they may enter') is right.
ʾănî ṣiwwêṯî limquddāšāy ... lᵉʾappî ʿallîzê gaʾăwāṯî: 'my consecrated ones', 'for my anger', 'my proudly exulting ones' (NRSV) are exact.

Canon-cited. qôl hāmôn behārîm dᵉmûṯ ʿam-rāḇ ... YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ mᵉp̄aqqēḏ ṣᵉḇāʾ milḥāmāh: participle 'is mustering' and the epithet/cognate play are rendered literally; nothing added. Lens check passed: the line is ASV/NRSV in substance.

Canon-cited, disputed vs ASV 'heaven'. bāʾîm mēʾereṣ merḥāq miqṣēh haššāmayim YHWH ûḵᵉlê zaʿmô lᵉḥabbēl kol-hāʾāreṣ: the horizon idiom parallel to 'a far land' is physical-register, so 'from the end of the skies' applies the ratified šāmayim rule; 'YHWH and the weapons of his indignation' is kept in apposition as the Hebrew has it. Lens check: the line neither strengthens nor weakens the canon's reading ('confins du ciel'), and the reception note is accurate (TBWTT 3 links 13:4-5, 14:13-17, 15:8-9 to Sodom).
Disputed vs ASV 'the Almighty'. kᵉšōḏ miššadday yāḇôʾ: transliterating 'Shaddai' keeps the šōḏ/šadday pun audible (NJPS precedent); defensible.
kol-yāḏayim tirpênāh wᵉḵol-lᵉḇaḇ ʾĕnôš yimmās: exact.
wᵉniḇhālû ṣîrîm waḥăḇālîm yōʾḥēzûn ... pᵉnê lᵉhāḇîm pᵉnêhem: exact; 'faces of flame' literal.
Disputed vs ASV 'land'. lāśûm hāʾāreṣ lᵉšammāh: from v. 9 the scope is cosmic (tēḇēl v. 11, sun/moon/stars v. 10, skies/earth v. 13), and 'the earth' is the reading of NRSV/NJPS and the commentators.
kôḵᵉḇê haššāmayim ûḵᵉsîlêhem: 'their constellations' (ASV/NRSV) for the generic plural of 'Orion' is standard; 'skies' is the physical register. Note's references (Job 9:9; 38:31; Amos 5:8) checked.
ûp̄āqaḏtî ʿal-tēḇēl rāʿāh ...: 'punish the world for its evil' is exact; ʿăwōnām 'their iniquity' under the central entry.
ʾôqîr ʾĕnôš mippāz wᵉʾāḏām mikketem ʾôp̄îr: 'a mortal … a human being' for ʾĕnôš / ʾāḏām is exact.
šāmayim ʾargîz wᵉṯirʿaš hāʾāreṣ mimmᵉqômāh: first-person Hiphil 'I will make the skies tremble' and cosmic 'earth' are exact.
wᵉhāyāh kiṣḇî muddāḥ ...: impersonal wᵉhāyāh kept ('And it shall be that'); exact.
kol-hannimṣāʾ yiddāqēr wᵉḵol-hannispeh yippôl beḥāreḇ: exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv/Qere verified: K tšglnh / Q tiššāḵaḇnāh. The qere is a euphemism for the same act, so rendering its sense ('ravished', ASV/NRSV) is faithful; 'lain with' would misreport the violence. Defensible.
hinnî mēʿîr ʿălêhem ʾeṯ-māḏāy: 'stirring up the Medes' is exact.
ûqᵉšāṯôṯ nᵉʿārîm tᵉraṭṭašnāh ...: exact (ASV/NRSV).

kᵉmahpēḵaṯ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-sᵉḏōm: overthrow formula kept with hāp̄aḵ ('overthrew'); 'God' for the formula is the book practice and NRSV/NJPS; the Genesis 'the Elohim' convention is correctly not imported.
lōʾ-ṯēšēḇ lāneṣaḥ ...: 'never be inhabited', 'no Arab will pitch his tent' exact.
ṣiyyîm, ʾōḥîm, bᵉnôṯ yaʿănāh, śᵉʿîrîm: ASV fauna kept, with NRSV 'goat-demons' honestly recorded; defensible since the list is of animals.
bᵉʾalmᵉnôṯāyw read as a by-form of ʾarmᵉnôṯāyw 'strongholds' (Targum, ASV 'castles', NRSV) without changing consonants; ʾiyyîm 'hyenas' (NRSV). Defensible.

glossaryReview.reasoning: direct verified: absolute, articular and indefinite ʾĕlōhîm, ʾēl and ʾĕlôah alternate inside one denial formula (44:6, 8; 45:21-22), so one English word is the accurate rendering, and capital/lower-case follows referent (YHWH vs idol), as ASV/NRSV do. The 45:18 vs 1 Kgs 18:39 divergence is handled as a verse-level flag (F3), not as a defect of the entry.

paragraphs.text: מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אָמֽוֹץ׃

i18n.en: The oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.
i18n.he: מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אָמֽוֹץ׃

notes.official: *maśśāʾ* heads the oracles against the nations (13:1; 14:28; 15:1 and on through ch. 23). The traditional “burden” (KJV, ASV) takes the word as *maśśāʾ* I, “load,” from *nśʾ* “carry.” The heading is now generally read as *maśśāʾ* II, “pronouncement,” from the idiom *nāśāʾ qôl* “lift up the voice” (HALOT; Weis, *A Definition of the Genre Maśśāʾ*, 1986). The line has “The oracle concerning Babylon,” with NRSV; NJPS has “pronouncement.” Jer 23:33–38 puns on the two senses, which shows that hearers felt the link, but it does not make “burden” the meaning of the heading (overlay `massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: עַ֤ל הַר־נִשְׁפֶּה֙ שְֽׂאוּ־נֵ֔ס הָרִ֥ימוּ ק֖וֹל לָהֶ֑ם הָנִ֣יפוּ יָ֔ד וְיָבֹ֖אוּ פִּתְחֵ֥י נְדִיבִֽים׃

i18n.en: On a bare mountain raise a signal; lift up the voice to them; wave the hand, that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
i18n.he: עַ֤ל הַר־נִשְׁפֶּה֙ שְֽׂאוּ־נֵ֔ס הָרִ֥ימוּ ק֖וֹל לָהֶ֑ם הָנִ֣יפוּ יָ֔ד וְיָבֹ֖אוּ פִּתְחֵ֥י נְדִיבִֽים׃

paragraphs.text: אֲנִ֥י צִוֵּ֖יתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁ֑י גַּ֣ם קָרָ֤אתִי גִבּוֹרַי֙ לְאַפִּ֔י עַלִּיזֵ֖י גַּאֲוָתִֽי׃

i18n.en: I myself have commanded my consecrated ones; I have also called my mighty men for my anger, my proudly exulting ones.
i18n.he: אֲנִ֥י צִוֵּ֖יתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁ֑י גַּ֣ם קָרָ֤אתִי גִבּוֹרַי֙ לְאַפִּ֔י עַלִּיזֵ֖י גַּאֲוָתִֽי׃

paragraphs.text: ק֥וֹל הָמ֛וֹן בֶּֽהָרִ֖ים דְּמ֣וּת עַם־רָ֑ב ק֠וֹל שְׁא֞וֹן מַמְלְכ֤וֹת גּוֹיִם֙ נֶֽאֱסָפִ֔ים יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְפַקֵּ֖ד צְבָ֥א מִלְחָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: The sound of a multitude in the mountains, like that of a great people! The sound of the uproar of kingdoms, of nations gathered together! YHWH of hosts is mustering a host for battle.
i18n.he: ק֥וֹל הָמ֛וֹן בֶּֽהָרִ֖ים דְּמ֣וּת עַם־רָ֑ב ק֠וֹל שְׁא֞וֹן מַמְלְכ֤וֹת גּוֹיִם֙ נֶֽאֱסָפִ֔ים יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְפַקֵּ֖ד צְבָ֥א מִלְחָמָֽה׃

notes.official: *YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ mᵉp̄aqqēḏ ṣᵉḇāʾ milḥāmāh* plays on one root: “YHWH of hosts is mustering a host for battle.” The epithet and the army it musters share the word *ṣāḇāʾ*. The line keeps the standard epithet (overlay `yhwh-tzevaot-hosts-isaiah`) and renders the participle *mᵉp̄aqqēḏ* “mustering” (*pqd* “muster, review troops”; ASV “mustereth”). The “sound of a multitude in the mountains” is the noise of the gathering armies of the nations. The canon quotes vv. 4–5 together; see the reception note at v. 5.

paragraphs.text: בָּאִ֛ים מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָ֖ק מִקְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם יְהוָה֙ וּכְלֵ֣י זַעְמ֔וֹ לְחַבֵּ֖ל כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: They come from a far land, from the end of the skies — YHWH and the weapons of his indignation — to destroy the whole land.
i18n.he: בָּאִ֛ים מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָ֖ק מִקְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם יְהוָה֙ וּכְלֵ֣י זַעְמ֔וֹ לְחַבֵּ֖ל כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official:
*miqṣēh haš-šāmayim* is the stock idiom for the farthest edge of the visible world, where sky meets earth (Deut 4:32; 30:4; Ps 19:7). It stands in parallel with *mē-ʾereṣ merḥāq* “from a far land.” Under the central *šāmayim* register rule the physical sky is “skies,” and the line has “from the end of the skies,” adjusting ASV’s singular “from the uttermost part of heaven.” The coming host is YHWH’s army, but the phrase locates its starting point at the horizon. It does not name YHWH’s dwelling, so the divine-realm register (“the heavens”) is not used here. *bāʾîm* “they come” has the mustered host of v. 4 as subject, with “YHWH and the weapons of his indignation” in apposition, as the Hebrew has it.

*kol-hā-ʾāreṣ* is rendered “the whole land” (ASV; central `eretz`): the oracle is set against Babylon, and the army comes to destroy that land. From v. 9 onward the horizon widens to the whole earth (see v. 9).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes 13:4–5 (“They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, even Yahweh, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land”) and reads it as the creators arriving from their own world with their weapons. It connects the passage with the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, to which it also relates 14:13–17 and 15:8–9. The line renders the horizon idiom by the central register rule and gives the host only the identity the Hebrew gives it.

paragraphs.text: הֵילִ֕ילוּ כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב י֣וֹם יְהוָ֑ה כְּשֹׁ֖ד מִשַּׁדַּ֥י יָבֽוֹא׃

i18n.en: Wail, for the day of YHWH is near; like destruction from Shaddai it comes.
i18n.he: הֵילִ֕ילוּ כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב י֣וֹם יְהוָ֑ה כְּשֹׁ֖ד מִשַּׁדַּ֥י יָבֽוֹא׃

notes.official: *kᵉšōḏ miš-šadday yāḇôʾ* “like destruction from Shaddai it comes” is a pun: *šōḏ* “devastation” and *šadday* sound alike. The identical line recurs at Joel 1:15. The line transliterates “Shaddai,” as NJPS does, which keeps the sound-play audible. ASV’s “the Almighty” goes back to the LXX/Vulgate *pantokratōr / omnipotens* tradition. The central `shaddai-eloah` entry (Job) is extended here for the name Shaddai only; ʾĕlôah at 44:8 is rendered “God” (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֖ן כָּל־יָדַ֣יִם תִּרְפֶּ֑ינָה וְכָל־לְבַ֥ב אֱנ֖וֹשׁ יִמָּס׃

i18n.en: Therefore all hands will grow slack, and every human heart will melt;
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּ֖ן כָּל־יָדַ֣יִם תִּרְפֶּ֑ינָה וְכָל־לְבַ֥ב אֱנ֖וֹשׁ יִמָּס׃

paragraphs.text: וְֽנִבְהָ֓לוּ ׀ צִירִ֤ים וַֽחֲבָלִים֙ יֹֽאחֵז֔וּן כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֖ה יְחִיל֑וּן אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ יִתְמָ֔הוּ פְּנֵ֥י לְהָבִ֖ים פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: and they will be dismayed; pangs and agonies will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor; each will look aghast at his neighbor; their faces are faces of flame.
i18n.he: וְֽנִבְהָ֓לוּ ׀ צִירִ֤ים וַֽחֲבָלִים֙ יֹֽאחֵז֔וּן כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֖ה יְחִיל֑וּן אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ יִתְמָ֔הוּ פְּנֵ֥י לְהָבִ֖ים פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם־יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א אַכְזָרִ֥י וְעֶבְרָ֖ה וַחֲר֣וֹן אָ֑ף לָשׂ֤וּם הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְחַטָּאֶ֖יהָ יַשְׁמִ֥יד מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: Behold, the day of YHWH is coming, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger, to make the earth a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם־יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א אַכְזָרִ֥י וְעֶבְרָ֖ה וַחֲר֣וֹן אָ֑ף לָשׂ֤וּם הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְחַטָּאֶ֖יהָ יַשְׁמִ֥יד מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

notes.official: From v. 9 the oracle widens from Babylon to a cosmic day of YHWH: the stars, sun and moon go dark (v. 10), YHWH punishes “the world” (*tēḇēl*, v. 11), and the skies and the earth shake (v. 13). In that register *hā-ʾāreṣ* is “the earth,” with NRSV and NJPS and the commentators (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*, 1997; Blenkinsopp, AB 19). ASV’s “the land” is recorded. The overlay entry `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`, written for the universal judgment of ch. 24, is extended to vv. 9 and 13.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־כוֹכְבֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּכְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א יָהֵ֖לּוּ אוֹרָ֑ם חָשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ בְּצֵאת֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖חַ לֹֽא־יַגִּ֥יהַ אוֹרֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: For the stars of the skies and their constellations will not give their light; the sun will be dark at its going forth, and the moon will not shed its light.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־כוֹכְבֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּכְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א יָהֵ֖לּוּ אוֹרָ֑ם חָשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ בְּצֵאת֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖חַ לֹֽא־יַגִּ֥יהַ אוֹרֽוֹ׃

notes.official: *kᵉsîlêhem*, literally “their Kesils,” is the plural of *kᵉsîl*, the name of the constellation Orion (Job 9:9; 38:31; Amos 5:8). In the plural it stands for the bright constellations generally, and the line keeps ASV and NRSV “their constellations.” The central `kimah-kesil-mazzarot-ayish` entry, which transliterates the names in Job’s catalogue, is not extended to this generic plural.

paragraphs.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י עַל־תֵּבֵל֙ רָעָ֔ה וְעַל־רְשָׁעִ֖ים עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ גְּא֣וֹן זֵדִ֔ים וְגַאֲוַ֥ת עָרִיצִ֖ים אַשְׁפִּֽיל׃

i18n.en: I will punish the world for its evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; I will put an end to the arrogance of the proud, and lay low the haughtiness of the ruthless.
i18n.he: וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י עַל־תֵּבֵל֙ רָעָ֔ה וְעַל־רְשָׁעִ֖ים עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ גְּא֣וֹן זֵדִ֔ים וְגַאֲוַ֥ת עָרִיצִ֖ים אַשְׁפִּֽיל׃

paragraphs.text: אוֹקִ֥יר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִפָּ֑ז וְאָדָ֖ם מִכֶּ֥תֶם אוֹפִֽיר׃

i18n.en: I will make a mortal rarer than fine gold, and a human being than the gold of Ophir.
i18n.he: אוֹקִ֥יר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִפָּ֑ז וְאָדָ֖ם מִכֶּ֥תֶם אוֹפִֽיר׃

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּן֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם אַרְגִּ֔יז וְתִרְעַ֥שׁ הָאָ֖רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ בְּעֶבְרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבְי֖וֹם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Therefore I will make the skies tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place, at the wrath of YHWH of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּן֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם אַרְגִּ֔יז וְתִרְעַ֥שׁ הָאָ֖רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ בְּעֶבְרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבְי֖וֹם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ כִּצְבִ֣י מֻדָּ֔ח וּכְצֹ֖אן וְאֵ֣ין מְקַבֵּ֑ץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־עַמּוֹ֙ יִפְנ֔וּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אַרְצ֖וֹ יָנֽוּסוּ׃

i18n.en: And it shall be that, like a hunted gazelle and like sheep with no one to gather them, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
i18n.he: וְהָיָה֙ כִּצְבִ֣י מֻדָּ֔ח וּכְצֹ֖אן וְאֵ֣ין מְקַבֵּ֑ץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־עַמּוֹ֙ יִפְנ֔וּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אַרְצ֖וֹ יָנֽוּסוּ׃

paragraphs.text: כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֖א יִדָּקֵ֑ר וְכָל־הַנִּסְפֶּ֖ה יִפּ֥וֹל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

i18n.en: Whoever is found will be thrust through, and whoever is caught will fall by the sword.
i18n.he: כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֖א יִדָּקֵ֑ר וְכָל־הַנִּסְפֶּ֖ה יִפּ֥וֹל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

paragraphs.text: וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֥ם יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם יִשַּׁ֙סּוּ֙ בָּֽתֵּיהֶ֔ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם תשגלנה [תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה׃]

i18n.en: Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered, and their wives ravished.
i18n.he: וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֥ם יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם יִשַּׁ֙סּוּ֙ בָּֽתֵּיהֶ֔ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם תשגלנה [תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה׃]

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere. The consonantal text has תשגלנה *tiššāḡalnāh* (from *šgl*, a coarse verb for sexual violation), and the Masoretes direct the reader to say *tiššāḵaḇnāh* “they shall be lain with” instead. The same substitution occurs at Deut 28:30 and Zech 14:2. The qere is read, as everywhere in this translation. Because it is a euphemism for the same act, the line gives its sense: “their wives ravished” (ASV, NRSV). A literal “lain with” would make the violence sound consensual (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: הִנְנִ֛י מֵעִ֥יר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת־מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁר־כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לֹ֣א יַחְשֹׁ֔בוּ וְזָהָ֖ב לֹ֥א יַחְפְּצוּ־בֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Behold, I am stirring up the Medes against them, who have no regard for silver, and as for gold, they take no delight in it.
i18n.he: הִנְנִ֛י מֵעִ֥יר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת־מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁר־כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לֹ֣א יַחְשֹׁ֔בוּ וְזָהָ֖ב לֹ֥א יַחְפְּצוּ־בֽוֹ׃

paragraphs.text: וּקְשָׁת֖וֹת נְעָרִ֣ים תְּרַטַּ֑שְׁנָה וּפְרִי־בֶ֙טֶן֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ עַל־בָּנִ֖ים לֹֽא־תָח֥וּס עֵינָֽם׃

i18n.en: Their bows will dash the young men to pieces; they will have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye will not spare children.
i18n.he: וּקְשָׁת֖וֹת נְעָרִ֣ים תְּרַטַּ֑שְׁנָה וּפְרִי־בֶ֙טֶן֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ עַל־בָּנִ֖ים לֹֽא־תָח֥וּס עֵינָֽם׃

paragraphs.text: וְהָיְתָ֤ה בָבֶל֙ צְבִ֣י מַמְלָכ֔וֹת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת גְּא֣וֹן כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־סְדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the splendor of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
i18n.he: וְהָיְתָ֤ה בָבֶל֙ צְבִ֣י מַמְלָכ֔וֹת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת גְּא֣וֹן כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־סְדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָֽה׃

notes.official: *kᵉ-mahpēḵaṯ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-sᵉḏōm wᵉʾeṯ-ʿămōrāh* is the fixed overthrow formula (Amos 4:11; Jer 50:40; cf. Deut 29:22). The line keeps “overthrew” under the central `mahapekhah-overthrowing-formula` entry, preserving the *hāp̄aḵ* lexeme of Gen 19:25, 29. Absolute *ʾĕlōhîm* is “God,” the book’s practice for every form of the word (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). The corpus’s “the Elohim” convention is scoped to the Genesis narrative and is not carried into the prophet’s allusion.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־תֵשֵׁ֣ב לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכֹּ֖ן עַד־דּ֣וֹר וָד֑וֹר וְלֹֽא־יַהֵ֥ל שָׁם֙ עֲרָבִ֔י וְרֹעִ֖ים לֹא־יַרְבִּ֥צוּ שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: It will never be inhabited, nor dwelt in from generation to generation; no Arab will pitch his tent there, and no shepherds will make their flocks lie down there.
i18n.he: לֹֽא־תֵשֵׁ֣ב לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכֹּ֖ן עַד־דּ֣וֹר וָד֑וֹר וְלֹֽא־יַהֵ֥ל שָׁם֙ עֲרָבִ֔י וְרֹעִ֖ים לֹא־יַרְבִּ֥צוּ שָֽׁם׃

paragraphs.text: וְרָבְצוּ־שָׁ֣ם צִיִּ֔ים וּמָלְא֥וּ בָתֵּיהֶ֖ם אֹחִ֑ים וְשָׁ֤כְנוּ שָׁם֙ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֔ה וּשְׂעִירִ֖ים יְרַקְּדוּ־שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: But desert creatures will lie down there, and their houses will be full of howling creatures; ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will dance there.
i18n.he: וְרָבְצוּ־שָׁ֣ם צִיִּ֔ים וּמָלְא֥וּ בָתֵּיהֶ֖ם אֹחִ֑ים וְשָׁ֤כְנוּ שָׁם֙ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֔ה וּשְׂעִירִ֖ים יְרַקְּדוּ־שָֽׁם׃

notes.official: The ruin-fauna of vv. 21–22 recur at 34:13–14. *ṣiyyîm* are “desert creatures,” *ʾōḥîm* (a hapax) “howling creatures,” and *bᵉnôṯ yaʿănāh* “ostriches” (ASV; some read “eagle-owls”). *śᵉʿîrîm* “hairy ones” is “wild goats” in ASV. NRSV has “goat-demons,” because the same word names the beings that receive illicit sacrifice at Lev 17:7 and 2 Chr 11:15. The line keeps “wild goats”: the context is a list of animals that move into a ruin, and the demonic sense is possible but not required (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*). The mythological reading is recorded here.

paragraphs.text: וְעָנָ֤ה אִיִּים֙ בְּאַלְמְנוֹתָ֔יו וְתַנִּ֖ים בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי עֹ֑נֶג וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ עִתָּ֔הּ וְיָמֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א יִמָּשֵֽׁכוּ׃

i18n.en: Hyenas will cry in its strongholds, and jackals in the palaces of delight; her time is near at hand, and her days will not be prolonged.
i18n.he: וְעָנָ֤ה אִיִּים֙ בְּאַלְמְנוֹתָ֔יו וְתַנִּ֖ים בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי עֹ֑נֶג וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ עִתָּ֔הּ וְיָמֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א יִמָּשֵֽׁכוּ׃

notes.official: MT *bᵉʾalmᵉnôṯāyw* “in its widows” is generally taken as a by-form or phonetic variant of *bᵉʾarmᵉnôṯāyw* “in its strongholds.” The interchange of *l* and *r* is attested, and the same form occurs at Ezek 19:7. The line follows the Targum, ASV (“castles”) and the modern versions without altering the consonantal text. *ʾiyyîm* “howlers” are “hyenas” (NRSV); ASV has “wolves.”
